title: He Made an FBI Agent Write Down His Own Friends' Names, and All 12 Died . . . (Episode 5)
caption:
In Death Note episode 5, Jack corners FBI agent Ray Penber on a Tokyo train and forces him to write down the names of all twelve FBI agents in Japan.
By morning every one of them is dead, and L's task force is down to six men. Follow for episode 6!

#deathnote #anime #animerecap #animeexplained #fyp
comment: Would you have obeyed Jack to save Naomi, like Ray did? Why?

segments.say: An FBI agent writes down the names of his own colleagues, and by morning all twelve of them are *dead*.
To see how it got here, go back to the bus, where Jack finally *cornered* the agent who was tailing him.
Ray flashes his FBI badge and begs Jack to keep it *secret*. Jack happily promises.
Jack walks away smiling. He has a name and a face now, and Ray has no idea.
Meanwhile, Ray goes home to his fiancée, Naomi, and he looks *shaken*.
He tells her a junkie hijacked his bus, then jumped off and got hit by a car.
Naomi doesn't buy it. A man dies right after Ray boards his bus? That's *suspicious*.
Ray cuts her off and makes her promise to stay out of the Kira case.
That night, back in his room, Jack picks up his pen. Ryuk asks if he's writing Ray's *name*.
Not yet. He'll wait a *week*, so nobody ties the death to him.
Patient. That's what makes him scary.
Meanwhile, another victim dies, and this time the suicide note mentions *gods of death*.
L reads it, stunned. Is Kira telling them that death gods are *real*?
A week later, Jack waits in a crowded train station, with Ryuk right beside him.
He tells Ryuk what his tests taught him. Write the death first, add the name *afterwards*, and it still works.
Even Ryuk didn't know that one.
Then Ray walks in, right on *time*.
Jack steps up behind him and whispers that if he turns around, he's *dead*.
Ray's blood runs cold. He knows that *voice* from somewhere.
To prove it, Jack points at a man sweeping the floor, and the man drops *dead*.
He only needs a face to kill, and this station is *full* of faces.

segments.text: Don't do it. I believe you. You're Kira.

segments.say: Then Jack hits him where it hurts. He knows all about *Naomi*.
Do exactly as he says, or Naomi and everyone Ray loves will *die*.
Ray takes an envelope with a tiny transceiver and an earpiece inside.
Ray never had a real choice.
Jack sends him onto the Yamanote line and watches from *close by*.
Over the earpiece, he asks how many agents are in Japan. Twelve. Four teams of *three*.
Then he hands Ray a stack of blank papers, and a laptop full of FBI *photos*.
Ray must write his boss's name at the top, then every other agent's name beneath.
Ray stares at the screen. Why would Kira need *him* to write names he already has?
Then comes the last order. Leave the envelope above your seat and ride on for thirty *minutes*.
Ray steps off the train, and that voice keeps nagging him. Whose *is* it?
Then he collapses on the platform, clutching his chest.
On the train, Jack just whispers *farewell*.
Cold. Even for Jack.
That's the twist. Every page Ray filled came from the *Death Note*, so he signed his friends' death warrants.
His boss died first, then the other eleven, all of *heart attacks*.
The FBI director calls Japan, learns all twelve are dead, and shuts the investigation *down*. Kira just won round one.
Then Jack's father learns that L sent the FBI to spy on his own *task force*.
His detectives are furious. They never trusted L, and now they have a *reason*.
L calmly points out the obvious. Kira will kill *anyone* who gets in his way.
At home, Naomi hears the news. Ray is *dead*.
That night, Jack's father calls a family meeting and admits he runs the Kira *case*.
His wife and daughter beg him to quit.
But the chief won't run.

segments.text: I will not sit back and let evil triumph.

segments.say: Jack tells his father he's proud, and swears he'll hunt Kira himself if anything happens.
He said that with a straight face.
At the task force, the chief offers everyone a last way out. Quit now, no *punishment*.
Out of the whole room, only five detectives stay.
Then L's message lights up a laptop. He trusts all *six* of them.
One detective explodes. Why trust a man who never shows his *face*?
So L offers something nobody has seen before. A real *meeting*.
One detective figures L was waiting all along, until the team shrank to men he could *trust*.
One man quits on the spot. The rest stay.
L sets the rules. Meet at his hotel at midnight, in two groups, thirty minutes *apart*.
L stands at the window and says he's ready to show his *face*.
Jack replays every move he made, hunting for a mistake. The real battle has only *begun*.
At midnight, the ones who stayed reach the door of the hotel room.
No face, just a voice saying *come in*.
But Ray's fiancée isn't giving up. Naomi tracks down the bus *driver* and asks who rode that day.
If Kira was on that bus, he lives *close by*.
And she is already closing in on *Kira*. Follow for episode 6!
